item.title: Trump dismisses reports of potential strikes on Iran, says “productive discussions” ongoing, no attacks before midterms
item.description: In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump dismisses reports of potential strikes on Iran, says “productive discussions” ongoing, no attacks before midterms In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved.  ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 22:25 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 22:25 IST

US President Donald Trump (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump on Thursday dismissed reports of possible fresh strikes against Iran, saying “productive discussions” are underway with Tehran and making clear that the United States will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved. He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon. “We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran. I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect, with Oil flowing in Record Numbers of Barrels through the Hormuz Strait (22 Million Barrels, last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran!), we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd. IRAN WILL NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON!” the post read. Trump's statement came a day after reports that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, potentially ahead of the midterms. Axios report that Trump had not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations against Iran, but that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for possible fresh strikes. According to Axios, citing US officials, the Pentagon instructed US Central Command several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran. The directive did not set a specific date for any potential strikes. US and Israeli officials cited by the publication said renewed combat operations could take place before the US midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, and possibly ahead of Israeli elections expected a week earlier. However, Trump's latest statement ruled out an attack before the US midterm elections while saying that discussions with Iran were continuing. Meanwhile, earlier in the day, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran would respond to a US peace proposal within the next few days, noting that the negotiations between Tehran and Washington remained ongoing and that messages were continuing to be exchanged through mediators. “The negotiation process is still ongoing and messages are being exchanged through mediators,” Araghchi said, as quoted by Iranian state media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB). The Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran had already presented its proposal, referred to as the “Seven-Day Plan”, and had received the US side's views on it. “We presented our plan, which we had presented under the title 'Seven-Day Plan', and we also heard the American side's views on it,” Araghchi said. “We are currently reviewing the views of the Americans and I think we will provide our response within the next few days,” he added. The ongoing diplomatic exchanges are linked to Tehran's proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz under a seven-day plan, which Araghchi presented last month during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Araghchi had said the timeline for the proposal would begin once the United States accepted it. According to Al Jazeera, he said Washington would need to take certain actions under the plan, which could be completed within four to five days. “If they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow,” Araghchi said. He said the required steps were already part of a memorandum of understanding and would not be difficult to implement. Under the proposal, if the US fulfilled the conditions, the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened on the sixth day, followed by renewed talks between Tehran and Washington on the seventh day. Trump had earlier rejected the proposed arrangement, according to The Wall Street Journal. (ANI)

item.title: US suspends Permanent labour certification program for Infosys, Wipro, Tata, Microsoft and others, cites abuse of H1B program
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday announced the suspension of Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting ...
item.content:encoded:
US suspends Permanent labour certification program for Infosys, Wipro, Tata, Microsoft and others, cites abuse of H1B program US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday announced the suspension of Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 21:29 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 21:29 IST

US VP JD Vance with Labour secretary Keith Sonderling and AG Todd Blanche on his left (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

In a far reaching move US Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling has announced that the US Government is suspending from the Permanent Labor Certification Program some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world which include Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini . The US Labour department attributed the suspension to multiple active federal investigations even as it also suspended US tech majors Microsoft and Adobe from the program. Speaking at a press conference on fighting visa fraud, US Vice President targeted the tech giants for alleged abuse of the H1B program "The H1-B visa program is meant to allow companies to bring in really the best of the best from outside the United States of America for positions that are completely impossible to fill with American workers. Unfortunately, the program has become rife with fraud," he said Attorney General Todd Blanche said, "This announcement today should send and does send a strong signal to every single employer in the United States that the Trump Administration will not tolerate discrimination against American workers." Vance further targeted tech giant Microsoft, alleging that the company had laid off American workers while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. Vance said Microsoft had laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. "Microsoft laid off last year, 6000 American workers at the same time the company benefited from 6300 H-1B visas and almost 3000 green cards. If you do the math for every worker that Microsoft laid off they replace that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants," he said. Vance said the administration's ongoing investigation had led to Microsoft's suspension from the programme. "That's a scandalous system we've allowed in this country for far too long but thanks to the work of this task force and the empowerment of the President of the United States we are going to stop because thanks to an ongoing investigation we suspend the program for Microsoft which means they will no longer able to take those visas and apply for permanent status," he added He also said the Trump administration wanted companies operating in the US to expand while prioritising American workers. "Our message to Microsoft in any other foreign or domestic corporation is simple. We want you to thrive in the United States of America. We want people to invest in the united states of America particularly the American technology sector, we are the biggest boosters of your industry. We want you to be able to grow and employ a lot of people but we want you to employ American workers. You are a great American company but you have to hire great American workers. You cannot lay off American workers and replace them with foreign indentured service," the US VP said. The US Labour secretary further said the department would not accept new applications or process pending permanent labor certification applications involving the companies. "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said. Sonderling said the companies named had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of H-1B visa approvals and permanent labor certifications. "Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H1B Visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications that's hundred and thousands of jobs that were taken from a American workers," the Labor Secretary said. The announcement comes a day after the US Department of Homeland Security proposed new fees for F-1 nonimmigrant students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system. Under the proposed rule announced on October 7, DHS would establish a USD 70,000 fee per F-1 nonimmigrant student for initial OPT and a USD 30,000 fee for any subsequent OPT. According to DHS, the proposal is aimed at reducing the flow of cheap labour into the United States, combating fraud and abuse, and making it easier for American citizens to compete in the job market. "Optional Practical Training was never meant to be a back door into the American workforce, a subsidy for cheap labor, or a prize for those who game the system," a DHS spokesperson said. "DHS is upskilling OPT to require foreign students to justify their worth to employers. American workers should not have to compete against a program that has been turned into a pipeline for cheap foreign labor." Under existing federal regulations, eligible F-1 students can participate in OPT when the employment is directly related to their major area of study. Students require a recommendation from their designated school official and must apply for employment authorisation with US Citizenship and Immigration Services. Eligible students can receive up to 12 months of OPT at each education level, while those who earn degrees in science, technology, engineering or mathematics fields may qualify for an additional 24-month extension. DHS said the proposed changes followed fraud and abuse identified by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program, including schemes involving problematic worksites and "pay-to-stay" visa arrangements. The proposed fees would be paid by SEVP-certified schools before designated school officials recommend students for OPT in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System and before students apply for employment authorisation with USCIS. DHS said the proposed fee would apply when schools recommend an F-1 student for any type of OPT and would not be tied to a particular employer. Collected fees would be deposited in the US Treasury. The department will accept public comments on the proposed rule from October 8 through November 9, while the Paperwork Reduction Act section will have a separate 60-day public comment period. (ANI)

item.title: AI-native networks, 6G to shape next phase of telecom, global leaders say at IMC 2026
item.description: India’s telecom sector is moving beyond expanding connectivity towards building AI-native networks, integrating intelligence into infrastructure and shaping global 6G standards, with technology ...
item.content:encoded:
AI-native networks, 6G to shape next phase of telecom, global leaders say at IMC 2026 India’s telecom sector is moving beyond expanding connectivity towards building AI-native networks, integrating intelligence into infrastructure and shaping global 6G standards, with technology leaders at India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 highlighting the need for programmable, secure and intelligent networks to support the next phase of the digital economy. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 20:51 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 20:51 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India’s telecom sector is moving beyond expanding connectivity towards building AI-native networks, integrating intelligence into infrastructure and shaping global 6G standards, with technology leaders at India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 highlighting the need for programmable, secure and intelligent networks to support the next phase of the digital economy. Ericsson CEO for South-East Asia, Oceania and India Andres Vicente said India’s rapid 5G adoption and investment in advanced networks have created a strong foundation for the next stage of digital growth. He said the transition to 5G Standalone would make networks more programmable and support differentiated connectivity, new AI-powered use cases and the eventual evolution towards 6G. GSMA Director General Vivek Badrinath said the focus is shifting from simply connecting people to determining what more than a billion connected people and businesses can do with digital infrastructure. “AI will be a major part of what comes next,” he said, stressing the importance of compute, models, data and skills alongside more intelligent and programmable networks. Qualcomm ISAG Chair Etienne Chaponniere highlighted another major shift, saying AI could become the new user interface as devices increasingly understand their surroundings and process information locally. He said greater on-device processing would reduce the need to send all data back to networks and have implications for the design and standardisation of future networks. TIM Head of European Affairs and Economic Studies Giacomo Robustelli said AI should also be viewed as an infrastructure revolution, with every new AI application increasing demand for connectivity, computing, storage and security. On 6G, Bharat 6G Alliance Chairman N.G. Subramaniam said the technology would go beyond faster speeds to make networks more intelligent, with communications and AI evolving together. He said India’s 6G development is being pursued in mission mode with government support and industry participation in research and innovation. C-DOT CEO Rajkumar Upadhyay meanwhile called for India’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem to move beyond production towards greater value creation through design, intellectual property and domestically developed equipment, alongside increased investment in security, quality, AI and cybersecurity. (ANI)

item.description: The three sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI)'s planned protest march to Islamabad last month demanding updates on Khan's health as well as his release from ...
item.content:encoded:
Imran Khan’s son says “no update” on “abducted” sisters of former PM; no contact with father for six months The three sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI)'s planned protest march to Islamabad last month demanding updates on Khan's health as well as his release from Adiala Jail, where the PTI founder has been incarcerated since August 2023. ANI | Updated: 08-10-2026 20:12 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 20:12 IST

Noreen Niazi (Left), Aleema Khanum (Centre) and Uzma Khanum, sisters of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan and founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party Imran Khan (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan’s son Kasim Khan on Thursday claimed that his three aunts remain “abducted” by the Pakistani authorities and that their family and lawyers have received no update about their condition or the reasons for their incarceration, while noting that he and his brother have had no contact with their father for more than six months. The three sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI)'s planned protest march to Islamabad last month demanding updates on Khan's health as well as his release from Adiala Jail, where the PTI founder has been incarcerated since August 2023. In a post on X, Kasim Khan linked the situation of his aunts with the continued lack of contact with his father, saying that he and his brother have not spoken to Imran Khan for more than six months. "Currently, my Aunties are still abducted. Family and lawyers have received no update on how they are, nor why they are incarcerated. Concerning my father, there is complete silence. My brother and I have had no contact with him for more than six months. We do not even know the true state of his health," the post read. He also referred to protests in Pakistan over the former prime minister's imprisonment, noting that the people were continuing to demand justice and the right to be heard. "Meanwhile, thousands of Pakistanis are peacefully taking to the streets to protest against his illegal and politically motivated imprisonment. However, the people of Pakistan have not given up. No barricade, intimidation or repression can muzzle the people’s demand for justice and their democratic right to be heard. There can be no lasting peace or stability while their democratic will is suppressed and their chosen leader remains behind bars,” Kasim Khan added. His remarks come a day after the families of Khan’s detained sisters, Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, approached the Lahore High Court, seeking permission for family members and lawyers to meet them. According to Dawn, Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar filed two separate civil miscellaneous applications in the pending writ petitions on the matter on behalf of Shah Raiz Khan, son of Aleema Khan, and Sakeena Niazi, daughter of Noreen Niazi. The pleas challenged the denial of meetings between the three sisters and their family members and lawyers, as well as access to medicines. The families have alleged that neither relatives nor legal counsel have been allowed to meet the detained women or provide them with medicines. The applications stated that medicines had been provided to the sisters on only one occasion and that no one had subsequently been allowed to meet them, Dawn reported. The pleas have raised concerns over the health of the detained sisters and sought directions from the Lahore High Court allowing their lawyers and family members to meet them and provide medicines, as reported by Dawn. Imran Khan's sisters were detained for 30 days ahead of the party's September 27 protest call. The detentions came amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad. The party had called for the demonstrations to demand Imran Khan's release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. On September 24, the Lahore High Court had declined a request to immediately suspend the notifications for the preventive detention of the sisters. (ANI)
